# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** About thirty or thirty-five  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Origin:** Toronto, Ontario  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and writer  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen is tall and broad-shouldered with thick brown hair and a finely-cut nose and chin. He has large, brilliant dark-gray eyes. Anne describes him as very well-looking and noting that he knows how to dress.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)_

## Personality

Owen possesses a pleasant voice and a delightful smile. He carries himself as someone who has experienced hardship in life. He inspires trust in others, possessing an empathetic nature that leads people to confide in him.

_Sources: [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)_

## Traits

- Empathetic  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>
- Trustworthy  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

## Abilities

- Magazine short story writing  <sub>[v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>
- Journalism and literary collaboration  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

## Goals

- To find the central idea and inspiration to write a novel  <sub>[v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>

## History

After recovering from typhoid fever in Toronto, Owen travelled to Four Winds on his doctor's orders and to visit the old place where his grandparents lived. Upon arriving, he sought the right central idea and leisure required to write a novel. He hit it off with Captain Jim, collaborating with him to write a biography based on Captain Jim's life experiences titled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim'. During his stay, Owen fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore and confided his feelings to Anne Blythe. Although he later travelled across the country to Vancouver, he returned to Four Winds in August to court Leslie, ultimately reaching an understanding with her in the garden.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P20](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0020), [v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030), [v4 c36 P27](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0027), [v4 c36 P49](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0049), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Selwyn, the schoolmaster who built the old house in Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Son of John Selwyn's eldest daughter and an Ontario man named Ford  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Suffered from a bad spell of typhoid fever in the spring  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Ordered by his doctor to spend time by the sea to recover his health  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’ve done a good deal of short story writing for the magazines, but I’ve never had the leisure that seems to be necessary for the writing of a book. With three months of liberty I ought to make a start, though—if I could only get the necessary motif for it—the SOUL of the book.  <sub>[v4 c23 P23](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0023)</sub>

> We’ll collaborate. You will give the soul and I the body. Oh, we’ll write a famous book between us, Captain Jim. And we’ll get right to work.  <sub>[v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>
